original_query: SELECT ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO FROM (SELECT ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO FROM EMP GROUP BY ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO HAVING SAL > 5000) AS t4 GROUP BY ROLLUP(ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO)
rewritten_query:
SELECT ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO
FROM EMP
WHERE SAL > 5000
GROUP BY ROLLUP(ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO);

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The HAVING SAL > 5000 condition operates on the grouping column SAL, so it is equivalent to a WHERE SAL > 5000 filter applied before grouping. Pushing it into WHERE avoids grouping rows that will be discarded.

The derived table t4 performs GROUP BY ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO solely as a deduplication step. Since the outer query already applies GROUP BY ROLLUP(ENAME, SAL, DEPTNO) with no aggregate functions, the ROLLUP itself suppresses duplicate combinations at every grouping level. The inner GROUP BY and derived table are therefore redundant and can be removed entirely, eliminating an extra aggregation pass.
No CTE is needed here — the query is simple and the derived table creates unnecessary overhead. Scanning EMP once with the pushed-down filter and applying ROLLUP directly is the most efficient form.
